native_result.query: In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants exhibits distinct prevalence styles across habitat types governed by landscape urbanization pressure, elevation, and hydrological/canopy structure: (1) In low-elevation semi-natural aquatic and littoral habitats (coastal, wetlands, riparian), gardening escapes exhibit high absolute prevalence and relative dominance (>53-56% of alien flora) over unintentional weeds due to their perennial and woody life forms; (2) In heavily anthropized habitats (urban, croplands), gardening species show high absolute presence in urban areas but a subordinate relative prevalence style (18-30% share) because physical disturbance and agricultural/trade vectors favor unintentional annual weeds; and (3) In closed-canopy natural forests, overall invasion is low but characterized by an exclusive gardening style (88-100% of alien occurrences, 0% unintentional) due to the shade tolerance and persistence of woody ornamental taxa.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Checked data schemas, delimiters, and summary statistics across all four datasets. 2. Computed absolute and relative prevalence metrics (richness, occupancy, alien proportion) for gardening, unintentional, and agriforest pathways across 10 habitat types. 3. Grouped habitats into broad ecological categories and executed contingency Chi-Square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. 4. Fitted multivariable logistic regressions (for plot-level occupancy across 632 plots) and Binomial GLMs (for relative pathway share across 191 invaded plots) testing elevation, climate, distance to streams/roads, and urban/cropland buffer scales (50m, 500m, 1000m). 5. Evaluated species functional traits (growth form, height, vegetative reproduction) from invasion_success_pathways.csv and temporal trends to provide mechanistic grounding. 6. Formulated and verified the data-grounded hypothesis.

sub_hypo.text: In low-elevation semi-natural aquatic and littoral habitats (coastal, wetlands, riparian), gardening escapes exhibit high absolute prevalence and relative dominance (>53-56% of alien flora) over unintentional weeds due to their perennial and woody life forms.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in low-elevation coastal, wetland, and riparian habitats in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Conditional on low elevation and aquatic or littoral habitat, gardening introductions have high absolute prevalence and a >53-56% share of alien flora, dominating unintentional introductions. This dominance is attributed to perennial and woody life forms.

sub_hypo.text: In heavily anthropized habitats (urban, croplands), gardening species show high absolute presence in urban areas but subordinate relative prevalence (18-30% share), because physical disturbance and agricultural/trade vectors favor unintentional annual weeds.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in heavily anthropized urban and cropland habitats in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Conditional on heavily anthropized habitat, gardening species have high absolute presence in urban areas but only an 18-30% relative share, subordinate to unintentional introductions. Physical disturbance and agricultural/trade introduction vectors are proposed to favor unintentional annual weeds; urban and cropland pressure are evaluated at 50 m, 500 m, and 1000 m buffer scales.

sub_hypo.text: In closed-canopy natural forests, overall invasion is low but characterized by an exclusive gardening style (88-100% of alien occurrences, 0% unintentional), due to the shade tolerance and persistence of woody ornamental taxa.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in closed-canopy natural forest habitats in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Conditional on closed-canopy natural forest habitat, total alien invasion is low, while gardening introductions constitute 88-100% of alien occurrences and unintentional introductions constitute 0%. This pathway composition is attributed to the shade tolerance and persistence of woody ornamental taxa.
